correctness.rationale: Expand Q_2 and Q_3 after y=(1+x)/2 and solve their derivative equations to obtain y2=(β+1)/(β+3) and y3=(β+2+sqrt(3(β+2)/(β+4)))/(β+5). The signed first extrema give exact amplitudes A2,A3. Their ratio under t=sqrt((β+2)/(β+4)) equals the stated elementary R(t). The logarithmic derivative lower bound uses log B>2(B-1)/(B+1), with F(q) increasing and F(sqrt3)=72-48sqrt3<0, so R increases strictly for β>-1. Its limit at -1 is 1/2 and the known β=-1/3 discrete inequality is strict, yielding exactly one crossing. High precision independently found β*=-0.36466584452339080365…, positive derivative samples, and signs on either side; this is corroboration. The separate y3>y2 proof follows by the explicitly positive squared identity for β>=1 and direct sign for -1<β<1.
